summary: Free guide of 12 principles for building reliable LLM agents, in the spirit of the classic 12 Factor App, from owning prompts to stateless design.

heroCommands.command: Start with Factor 1 in the repo's content folder

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: 12-Factor Agents is a written guide to building production-grade LLM applications. It sets out twelve principles, such as turning natural language into tool calls, owning your prompts and context window, treating tools as structured outputs, contacting humans through tool calls, owning your control flow, keeping agents small and focused, and making your agent a stateless reducer.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many agent frameworks get you to a demo but not to reliable software. This guide explains the engineering patterns that make agents dependable in production.
whoFor: Developers building LLM agents for real users
Engineering leads choosing an agent architecture
Anyone moving from prototype to production
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for clear, framework-independent principles you can apply to any agent code.

overview: The README gives a short version of the 12 factors with a link to a page for each, plus background on how agents evolved from code to DAGs to loops.
Read the factors in order, or jump to the one you need, such as owning your context window or compacting errors into context.
Written content is CC BY-SA 4.0 and code is Apache 2.0.
